problem:
Find the smallest positive integer $x$ (measured in degrees) such that
\[\tan (x - 160^{\circ}) = \frac{\cos50^{\circ}}{1 - \sin50^{\circ}}.\]
solution:
We can write $\frac{\cos 50^\circ}{1 - \sin 50^\circ} = \frac{\sin 40^\circ}{1 - \cos 40^\circ}.$  By the half-angle formula,
\[\frac{\sin 40^\circ}{1 - \cos 40^\circ} = \frac{1}{\tan 20^\circ} = \tan 70^\circ.\]We want
\[\tan (x - 160^\circ) = \tan 70^\circ,\]so $x - 160^\circ - 70^\circ = 180^\circ n$ for some integer $n,$ or
\[x = 180^\circ n + 230^\circ.\]Taking $n = -1$ to get the smallest positive value, we get $x = \boxed{50^\circ}.$
response_with_ans:
From the angle subtraction formula,
\[\tan (x - 160^\circ) = \frac{\tan x - \tan 160^\circ}{1 + \tan x \tan 160^\circ}.\]Also,
\begin{align*}
\frac{\cos 50^\circ}{1 - \sin 50^\circ} &= \frac{\cos 50^\circ}{1 - \sin 50^\circ} \cdot \frac{1 + \sin 50^\circ}{1 + \sin 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\cos 50^\circ (1 + \sin 50^\circ)}{1 - \sin^2 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\cos 50^\circ + \sin 50^\circ \cos 50^\circ}{\cos^2 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{1}{\cos 50^\circ} + \frac{\sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} \\
&= \sec 50^\circ + \tan 50^\circ \\
&= \frac{1}{\cos 50^\circ} + \frac{\sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{1 + \sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\cos 40^\circ + \sin 50^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ + \cos 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\sin 130^\circ + \sin 50^\circ}{\cos 40^\circ + \cos 50^\circ} \\
&= \frac{2 \sin 90^\circ \cos 40^\circ}{2 \cos 45^\circ \cos 5^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 5^\circ} \\
&= \frac{\sin 50^\circ}{\cos 5^\circ} \\
&= \tan 50^\circ.
\end{align*}Hence, we want to solve the equation
\[\frac{\tan x - \tan 160^\circ}{1 + \tan x \tan 160^\circ} = \tan 50^\circ.\]This simplifies to $\tan x = \tan 210^\circ,$ so $x = \boxed{210}.$
